body:
Updrafts rise through the clear part of the environment, which is cooler and denser than the environment mean, whose temperature includes the latent heat of the condensate in the cloudy part. With 1M microphysics and `PrognosticEDMFX`, the updraft buoyancy (`ᶜρ_diffʲs`) is taken against `ρ + Δρ`, where `Δρ` (`updraft_reference_density_excess`) is the density excess of the environment with the fraction `f_ev (1 − cf⁰)` of its cloud liquid and ice, and their latent heat, removed at fixed pressure and total water. Here `cf⁰` is the environment cloud fraction of the SGS closure, and `f_ev` = `edmf_buoyancy_clear_env_weight` (default `0`, bit-identical to main). `Δρ` vanishes in clear and in overcast environments; with `f_ev = 1`, the reference is the mixture `(cf⁰)²` cloudy and `1 − (cf⁰)²` clear of the two-part environment, so `Δρ ≈ cf⁰ (1 − cf⁰) (ρ_clear − ρ_cloudy)`, largest in broken cloud.

- The reference enters the updraft momentum and area solves and the entrainment closures. The pressure work in the updraft `mse` equation adds `ᶜρ_ref_excess / ρʲ` back and keeps the grid-mean density: the extra buoyancy is an updraft–environment force pair classed with the pressure closure, which preserves the PROPHET domain-decomposition identities (see the reference-density note in `docs/src/prophet.md`).
- The draft closures run after the cloud-fraction update, reading the environment cloud fraction (new field `ᶜcloud_fraction⁰`) of the same state, so restarts are reproducible. The Picard predictor evaluates `Δρ` once, at the stage-entering state.
- `toml/prognostic_edmfx_1M.toml` and `toml/prognostic_edmfx_1M_mlcloud.toml` set `f_ev = 1`, which changes the 1M EDMFX column jobs, `larcform1_1M_prognostic_edmfx`, and the 1M aquaplanet, AMIP target, and benchmark configurations; the 2M RICO job ignores the weight. Reference counter bumped to 474.
- Tests: unit tests for `Δρ` (exact zero limits, sign, linearization, ice against liquid) and the parameter range, and a 1M EDMFX DYCOMS RF01 column restart case that checks exact restart reproduction with nonzero `Δρ`. Docs: the reference-density note in `prophet.md` and a tail-entrainment paragraph in `prophet_closures.md`.

Peeled off `ts/Sc-Cu-rev`.
title: Reference updraft buoyancy to the clear part of the environment

body:
This PR changes how we built the vector of diagnostics by avoiding splatting. Splatting calls `Base.vect` which specializes on every element in the lists being splatted. This is avoided by appending to a vector instead.

I ran this script

```julia
import ClimaAtmos as CA, ClimaDiagnostics, Dates
import ClimaUtilities.TimeManager: ITime

model = CA.AtmosModel(CA.SphereGrid(Float32);
    microphysics_model = CA.NonEquilibriumMicrophysics1M(),
    radiation_mode = CA.RRTMGPI.AllSkyRadiationWithClearSkyDiagnostics(),
    turbconv_model = CA.PrognosticEDMFX(; prognostic_tke = true, area_fraction = 1.0f-5))
start_date = Dates.DateTime(2010)
t_start, duration = promote(ITime(0; epoch = start_date), ITime(732 * 86400; epoch = start_date))
writer = ClimaDiagnostics.Writers.DictWriter()

@time diags = CA.Diagnostics.default_diagnostics(model, duration, start_date, t_start; output_writer = writer, topography = true)
```

and got the following timings:

```julia-repl
# main branch
julia> @time diags = CA.Diagnostics.default_diagnostics(model, duration, start_date, t_start; output_writer = writer, topography = true)
  8.880688 seconds (22.43 M allocations: 1.181 GiB, 2.53% gc time, 99.76% compilation time)

# this PR
julia> @time diags = CA.Diagnostics.default_diagnostics(model, duration, start_date, t_start; output_writer = writer, topography = true)
  3.001751 seconds (4.21 M allocations: 221.945 MiB, 2.42% gc time, 99.80% compilation time)
```
title: Build list of diagnostics without splatting

body:
Adds a floor on the width of the truncated-Gaussian cloud-fraction closure in proportion to the subsaturation deficit `δ_sub = max(0, −μ_S)`:

```
σ_aug² = (α σ_S)² + (ε_rel δ_sub)² + σ_abs²
```

Where the condensate falls short of equilibrium, the variance fidelity narrows `α σ_S` in proportion to `q_c`, so the cloud fraction stays fixed as the condensate decreases (about 9% at a deficit of one standard deviation). The floor bounds the normalized condensate by `q_c / (ε_rel δ_sub)`, so the cloud fraction of subsaturated air vanishes with its condensate. The term vanishes at saturation, and condensate in equilibrium keeps its Gaussian cover.

- New provisional parameter `cloud_fraction_eps_rel` (`ε_rel`). Its default `0` supersedes the ClimaParams value `0.02` and reproduces the current results.
- `toml/default_parameters.toml` sets `ε_rel = 0.05`, so the floor applies to the moist jobs that read it with the `quadrature` cloud model; the reference counter is bumped.
- `docs/src/prophet_closures.md` states the cloud-fraction relation, the two floors, and the variance-fidelity factors; unit tests cover the width, the bound, and the documented numbers.
title: Add a subsaturation-deficit floor of the cloud-fraction width
